directAnswer: To troubleshoot a subnet mask, verify that the subnet mask matches the intended network configuration and check for any IP address conflicts within the subnet.
summary: This guide provides steps to troubleshoot issues related to subnet masks in networking.

sections.heading: Understanding Subnet Masks
sections.body: A subnet mask defines the network portion of an IP address. It is crucial to ensure that devices within the same network have matching subnet masks to communicate effectively.

sections.heading: Common Issues
sections.body: Some common issues include incorrect subnet mask settings, IP address conflicts, and devices being on different subnets.

sections.heading: Verifying Settings
sections.body: Check the subnet mask settings on your devices to ensure they are consistent. Use commands like 'ipconfig' on Windows or 'ifconfig' on Linux to view these settings.

steps.title: Check IP Configuration
steps.detail: On Windows, open Command Prompt and type 'ipconfig'. On Linux, use 'ifconfig' or 'ip addr'. Verify the subnet mask displayed.

steps.title: Ping Test
steps.detail: Perform a ping test to another device on the same subnet. If the ping fails, check the subnet mask and IP address of both devices.

steps.title: Review Network Settings
steps.detail: Access your router or switch settings to ensure the subnet mask is configured correctly. This may vary by device.

faqs.question: What happens if my subnet mask is incorrect?
faqs.answer: An incorrect subnet mask can prevent devices from communicating with each other, leading to network connectivity issues.

faqs.question: How do I find my subnet mask?
faqs.answer: You can find your subnet mask by using the 'ipconfig' command on Windows or 'ifconfig' on Linux.

faqs.question: Can subnet masks vary between devices?
faqs.answer: Yes, subnet masks can vary if devices are configured for different networks. Ensure they match for proper communication.

caveats: Ensure that all devices on the same network segment have the same subnet mask.
Check for overlapping IP ranges when configuring multiple subnets.
